# JusPrin production documentation

This directory is the canonical starting point for production work on `jusprin-newui`. It preserves the durable product and engineering decisions from `jusprin-v2-poc` without importing the POC's temporary windows, probes, static mocks, generated evidence, or environment-gated startup paths.

Read these documents in order:

1. [Product definition](product-definition.md) — the human/agent boundary, required product surfaces, workflow, and visibility rules.
2. [Production architecture](architecture.md) — the selected native/WebView architecture, ownership rules, component boundaries, and implementation sequence.
3. [Engineering and verification method](engineering-method.md) — how to assess risk and what evidence is required before calling a feature complete.
4. [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) — known Orca behaviors, lifecycle traps, event and history constraints, and testing lessons.
5. [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md) — required before changing any OrcaSlicer-owned file: where a seam belongs, why additive beats rewritten, how to leave a conflict that resolves correctly, and what evidence a change must record.
6. [Design system](design-system.md) — brand behavior, semantic UI tokens, typography, spacing, accessibility, and asset rules.
7. [POC reference](poc-reference.md) — exact pointers to the spike-only documents, code, commits, logs, screenshots, and generated brand artifacts left on `jusprin-v2-poc`.
8. [Tool extension guide](mcp-tool-extension-guide.md) — shared Agent/MCP contracts, process-settings workflow, execution and verification requirements.
9. [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md) — managed project storage, migration, restore, export, retention, and failure behavior.

Printer UI without hardware (Bambu in-process fake; control file; isolated app): [Fake Bambu README](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md). Print-host (Klipper/Moonraker) simulation stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter`.

## Governing decisions

- JusPrin is an AI-piloted 3D-printing product built on OrcaSlicer, not a replacement slicing engine.
- OrcaSlicer's C++ model, slicing pipeline, viewport, geometry operations, project serialization, and undo stack remain authoritative.
- The production application stays native C++/wxWidgets/OpenGL. The Agent conversation uses a local React/TypeScript application inside `wxWebView`.
- JavaScript renders state and submits typed commands; it never owns editable Orca project state.
- When logic could live in either C++ or a React page, it goes in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++: it touches Orca state, enforces a limit or boundary the app must guarantee, has to work without a page, or needs a thread or lifetime the page lacks. See [Where logic goes](architecture.md#where-logic-goes-the-page-first).
- Product policy lives in fork-owned files. OrcaSlicer-owned files receive only small, product-neutral, additive seams — every line changed there is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase.
- The user owns physical facts, object meaning, desired outcomes, privacy and legal decisions, and starting consequential physical actions.
- The production branch must not import experimental POC behavior merely because it demonstrated feasibility. Use the POC as evidence and reimplement through stable production boundaries.

## Source lineage

`jusprin-newui` and `jusprin-v2-poc` share base commit `8500fcdcca` (`v2.4.2`). The POC reference is pinned to final POC commit `9bba835b92`, so future changes to branch names do not make the historical evidence ambiguous.
----
     307 /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin-worktrees/composer-redesign/agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md

# JusPrin design system

**Status:** Canonical product and brand guidance for `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin should make advanced 3D printing feel immediate: a confident path from model to machine that removes detours without hiding control. The product should feel focused, assured, inventive, and approachable. Its voice is direct, capable, and optimistic—never cute, cryptic, or over-engineered.

The original JusPrin logo was supplied by the user and restored from repository revision `6eecb78b19`. The purple gradient endpoints were verified from the source SVG. Positioning language in the POC brand kit is proposed product direction, not an externally sourced market claim.

## Brand behavior

- **Focused:** every element earns its place.
- **Assured:** guidance is calm and actions are decisive.
- **Inventive:** the product is technical without being intimidating.
- **Approachable:** use plain language instead of slicer jargon where possible.
- Make the next action obvious. Brand behavior should feel as focused as the visual system.

The logo suggests an end-to-end journey through its orbit, precision and momentum through the crossing diagonals, flexible control through the open circle, and technical confidence softened by warmth through the purple gradient.

Write the name exactly as **JusPrin**: capital J and P, no space, never all caps in body copy. Use surrounding text color for the name in ordinary copy; do not force a gradient into small text.

## Logo use

The primary expressions are the horizontal lockup, the compact product mark, and the text wordmark. Use the compact mark for application icons and small product contexts.

- Clear space: at least one quarter of the mark width on every side.
- Minimum digital mark: 24 px.
- Minimum digital horizontal lockup: 120 px.
- Minimum printed mark: 8 mm.
- Minimum printed lockup: 32 mm.
- Below these sizes, use the mark alone and verify that the orbit arcs remain distinct.

Always use the original artwork, preserve its aspect ratio and components, maintain clear space, and place it on White, Mist, Ink, or another quiet solid field. Do not stretch, rotate, redraw, arbitrarily recolor, outline, shadow, separate, or place it directly over visual noise. Monochrome is allowed only when required. If the center crossing or orbit loses clarity, increase size, contrast, or space.

## Brand palette

| Name | Value | Use |
|---|---:|---|
| Orbit | `#3A2D64` | Primary brand color and decisive light-mode action |
| Violet | `#6F4F84` | Secondary brand color, headings, and essential boundaries |
| Bloom | `#CE84B7` | Expressive accent and dark-mode primary action |
| Ink | `#17131F` | Primary text and dark canvas |
| Mist | `#F6F2F7` | Soft canvas and grouped surfaces |
| Trace | `#E8DFEB` | Light dividers and quiet structure |
| White | `#FFFFFF` | Primary light canvas |
| Success | `#2D6A55` | Light success state |
| Danger | `#B44757` | Light error or destructive state |
| Warning | `#D49A2A` | Light warning state |

The signature gradient runs from Orbit to Bloom. Reserve it for the original logo, splash, onboarding, and rare hero moments. Do not use it as ordinary product chrome.

Product code must resolve colors through semantic tokens in `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; raw palette values are not a component API.

## Semantic color behavior

Dark mode is a semantic remapping, not a visual inversion. Preserve hierarchy, density, and geometry while choosing the dark value for the same named intent.

Core mappings include:

| Token | Light | Dark | Purpose |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `surface.canvas` | `#FFFFFF` | `#17131F` | Main application background |
| `surface.subtle` | `#F6F2F7` | `#211B2A` | Sidebars and grouped settings |
| `surface.raised` | `#FFFFFF` | `#2B2336` | Dialogs, menus, elevated panels |
| `text.primary` | `#17131F` | `#F6F2F7` | Headings, values, body copy |
| `text.secondary` | `#5F5767` | `#CFC5D3` | Descriptions and secondary labels |
| `border.subtle` | `#E8DFEB` | `#4B3E57` | Dividers and quiet structure |
| `border.strong` | `#6F4F84` | `#7D6A8D` | Focus and essential boundaries |
| `action.primary` | `#3A2D64` | `#CE84B7` | Decisive primary action |
| `action.primary.hover` | `#4B3A77` | `#D99AC5` | Pointer hover |
| `action.primary.pressed` | `#2B214F` | `#B76CA0` | Pressed or active state |

The JSON token file is authoritative and contains the complete action, status, selected-surface, disabled, text, and component values.

## Typography

Product UI uses fonts already shipped by OrcaSlicer:

- HarmonyOS Sans SC Regular for body and controls.
- HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold for hierarchy and actions.
- NanumGothic for Korean and Sarabun for Thai where the existing application requires them.
- The system GUI font as fallback.
- The system monospace font only for code: API keys, file paths, commands, config text, and IDs such as hashes. Never for names, words, or measurements.

HarmonyOS Sans SC draws every digit at the same width, so times, percentages,
and other values that change in place do not shift in the UI face; they do
not need the monospace one. The native shell has no monospace text.

Never require Menlo or another platform-specific face. The broader marketing brand kit used Avenir Next for display and marketing; that is not the cross-platform product UI requirement.

| Role | Size/line height in DIP | Weight |
|---|---:|---|
| Page title | 24/30 | Bold |
| Section | 18/24 | Bold |
| Body and control | 14/20 | Regular |
| Body bold | 14/20 | Bold |
| Body small | 13/18 | Regular |
| Body small bold | 13/18 | Bold |
| Label | 12/16 | Regular |
| Label bold | 12/16 | Bold |
| Dense metadata | 10/14 | Regular |
| Dense metadata bold | 10/14 | Bold |
| Code (system monospace) | 12/16 | Regular |

The bold pairs exist for emphasis inside a run of the same size (a primary
action beside secondary ones, the current row of a menu, a chip's name beside
its detail). Code is a single role, `typography.code`, whatever size the
text around it is.

## Layout and geometry

Design for a dense, native, high-DPI desktop application on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use device-independent pixels (DIP), not physical pixels. Verify 100%, 150%, and 200% scaling.

- Spacing scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, and 48 DIP.
- Standard control radius: 4 DIP, matching OrcaSlicer's own controls.
- Compact or branded action radius: 8 DIP.
- Container radius: 8 DIP, for grouped panels and cards, matching OrcaSlicer's `StaticBox` default.
- Window action and large-dialog radius: 12 DIP.
- Capsule radius: `pill`, for status chips and progress tracks whose shape is
  the full height. Menu rows sit inset 4 DIP inside the popover and carry the
  standard radius, so a hovered row reads as a control inside the panel
  rather than a stripe across it.
- Reserve 16–24 DIP radii for onboarding and marketing, not the main application shell.

Avoid web-only assumptions such as oversized controls, blur-heavy or glass surfaces, fixed physical pixels, and platform-specific fonts.

## Components and states

Use the existing native component density and Lucide `v1.47.0` SVG artwork for generic functional icons. Pin the artwork in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons` and use the same SVG geometry in Figma, the React pages, and the native shell; a package or plugin alone is not the cross-surface source of truth. Keep the JusPrin mark and product-specific symbols custom. Functional clarity comes before logo-derived decoration.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.
- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate, warning, and info glyphs sit inside a row of Label or Metadata text, 14 to 16 DIP tall, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. The card's disclosure chevron is an ordinary 16 DIP icon. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.
- Shared progress track: 4 DIP from `component.progress.height`; PrinterCard and Agent activity use this role rather than owning separate track heights.
- Orbit motif: progress, connection, or active workflow; verify stroke clarity at output size.
- Directional accent: at most one diagonal for momentum; avoid decorative competing angles.
- Compact button: 8×3 DIP padding, 8 DIP radius, dense metadata text.
- Window button: minimum 58×24 DIP, 12 DIP radius, 12 DIP text.
- Choice control: minimum 100×32 DIP, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Parameter control: 120×26 DIP, 4 DIP radius, 14 DIP text.
- Icon button: 26×26 DIP, 16 DIP icon, 4 DIP radius.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.
- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the Figma frames on the Plates & Project Pane page.
- Agent-pane divider: transparent 8 DIP pointer target with a centered 2 DIP line; the line changes from subtle to strong on hover and to the primary action color while dragging.
- Agent-pane width: minimum 320 DIP; its maximum follows the window width while preserving at least 320 DIP for the workspace.
- Printer setup, connecting, printer settings, and filament settings help use the same temporary conversation layer over the originating workspace. The underlying Home, Prepare, or Preview screen stays selected and constructed so Back returns to it. The conversation keeps the centered content width from `component.printerSetup.contentWidth` and the existing task header controls; manual settings remain available from that header. The saved project Agent pane remains a separate persistent conversation.
- Agent-pane collapse: a 26 DIP icon button in the header, left of the overflow button, whose glyph fills its right-hand column while the pane is open and empties it while the pane is closed. Double-clicking the divider closes the pane. Dragging it does not: a drag only sizes the pane and stops at its 320 DIP minimum, so aiming for a narrow pane never takes the conversation off the screen. There is no keyboard shortcut, no animation, and no automatic reopening; the pane is hidden, never destroyed, so its conversation survives. Reopening restores the width it last held.

Every interactive component must define normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focused, success, warning, and error states where relevant. Status must combine color with an icon and plain-language label.

## Accessibility

- Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; 3:1 is allowed only for large text.
- Essential control boundaries and state indicators require 3:1.
- Keyboard focus uses a visible 2 DIP ring and may not rely on a fill-color change alone.
- Orbit on White measures 12.07:1 in the source design system.
- Bloom on Ink measures 6.62:1.
- Light secondary text measures 6.89:1 on White.
- Dark secondary text measures 10.95:1 on Ink.

## Writing UI code

Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from Figma and from
the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.

1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
   value that exists in Figma but not in the roles or scales is a design
   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
5. **Read the code on `jusprin-newui`, not old commit messages or Figma,
   when they disagree.** The header's chip and menu dimensions were once
   changed to match Figma and reverted because they looked worse; the
   token file records what stayed.
6. **Run the guards before calling UI work done:** `brand_tokens_tests`,
   `shell_theme_tests`, and `npm test` in `AgentUI`. Then look at the surface
   in the running app; the guards prove the code went through the tokens,
   not that the result looks right.
7. **Upstream files are off limits for style.** OrcaSlicer's own screens are
   retinted through the hooks `BrandPalette.cpp` installs and nothing else;
   see [Fork stewardship](fork-stewardship.md). Their radii and fonts stay
   OrcaSlicer's until the surface is replaced.

## Runtime application in the native app

The token file is applied to the running application in three layers. All
three read `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`; none of them carries a
color literal of its own, and the whole layer touches OrcaSlicer code in only
three small, additive seams plus one attachment point.

1. **Fork-owned surfaces** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/*`, the React Agent
   page) resolve every style through the token file, not only color.
   - Native: `ShellTheme` exposes `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for
     the radius and spacing scales and the per-component sizes, `font(role)`
     for the type roles above. It is loaded once, by `Brand/BrandPalette.cpp`, and passed
     by reference into every shell widget. Widgets that paint themselves read
     it directly; a stock `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button`
     is dressed through the three functions in `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, so no
     fork-owned C++ file names an OrcaSlicer font preset or writes a radius as
     a number. `tests/jusprin/test_shell_theme.cpp` checks the parse and the
     fonts.
   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as
     `--<group>-<name>` on every appearance change, and once at startup the
     radii as `--radius-<name>` and each type role as a complete `font`
     shorthand, `--font-<role>` in the UI face, plus `--font-code` for the one
     monospace role. The stylesheet may only say `var(--…)` for color, radius,
     and type; `AgentUI/src/styles.test.ts` reads the stylesheet from disk and
     fails on any literal, and on any spacing value off the scale.
   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its
     icons are the `currentColor` SVGs in `resources/jusprin/ui/icons`,
     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
     translucent rounded rectangles.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
     switches at once.
   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
     color.
   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"
     without touching a string or macro in upstream code. Attribution strings
     in About are excluded by the script.
   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles
     reference it.

`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` fails the build if a token edit breaks the
contrast rules above or leaves a token in one mode without its counterpart in
the other. The same test guards the radius, spacing, and type scales: the
`dimension.radius`, `dimension.space`, and `typography.roles` tables must match
the values in this document exactly, `typography.code` must stay a single
12/16 role, every component radius must be one of the scale values, and every
button recipe must name a type role rather than a raw size.

Known gaps, all deliberate: ImGui panels and canvas notifications keep the
teal accent; the first-run setup wizard (an OrcaSlicer HTML page) is
Orca-branded until JusPrin's own onboarding replaces it; the About dialog
links to the OrcaSlicer website; vendor printer profiles other than the
generic ones keep their own plate textures; dark mode and the Preview canvas
were not visually verified.

## Design handoff requirements

Every high-fidelity product frame must:

1. Define each application screen in one canonical appearance mode. Do not
   create paired light and dark screen frames. The other mode must be
   deterministically derived by the design system from the same semantic token
   names, component variants, geometry, content, and interaction state. Verify
   light/dark differences in the design-system primitives and semantic mappings
   rather than duplicating every application screen.
2. State the mode, viewport, component variants, keyboard focus, and any deliberate exception.
3. Use DIP, native density, and the standard radius scale.
4. Use HarmonyOS Sans SC for product UI, and monospace only for code (Figma's Code style uses Roboto Mono as a stand-in for the system font).
5. Show normal, hover, pressed, disabled, focus, error, warning, and success states as applicable.
6. Test long filenames, localized labels, dense settings, empty states, and narrow windows.
7. Use the original logo and existing functional icon system.
8. Label and justify any value that is not in the token files.

The POC decks, rendered examples, horizontal lockup PNG, and generation sources remain available for visual-reference work through [POC reference](poc-reference.md). They are not runtime dependencies.

Phase 2 (read-only deterministic Agent) implemented on `jusprin-newui` on 2026-08-30.

- Native bridge: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/` — `AgentHost` (GUI-free coordinator, owns the authoritative conversation; streaming advances only via `pump_stream()`), `DeterministicMockAgent` (`/fail`, `/flaky`, `/slow` scenarios), `AgentWebView` (wx transport + internal-error surface).
- React page: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/` (npm package). `npm run build` writes the committed single-file bundle `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html`; the C++ build never needs Node. Rebuild + recommit the bundle whenever AgentUI changes.
- Shared protocol source: `resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json` — both `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` and the vitest suite assert their constants against it. Bump the version there and in `AgentProtocol.hpp`/`protocol.ts` together.
- Workspace contract gained `WorkspaceSetup` (project/printer/filament) and per-plate `sliced`; adding fields to `WorkspacePlate` breaks brace-initializers in `tests/workspace/test_workspace_contract.cpp`.
- Agent availability toggle: app config `jusprin_agent` = "0" → clean unavailable state (distinct from bridge errors by design).
- Deliberate gaps: preset changes only refresh Agent context at the next workspace event (needs a preset-changed seam, noted since Phase 1); Windows/Linux WebView untested.
- Evidence record: was `agent-docs/jusprin/agent-webview-phase-2.md`; removed 2026-08-30 at Kenny's request — recover it from git history or the Phase 2 commit message. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[jusprin-v2-poc-rebase-not-merge]].
===== agent-bridge-phase-5.md
---
name: agent-bridge-phase-5
description: "Phase 5 (attachments) implementation — protocol v4, storage, host decode, native import seam, React UI, and the deliberate tradeoffs."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 05ae687e-7468-4101-ba4b-f0017c8876c5
  modified: 2026-09-01T07:39:53.003Z
---

Phase 5 (Attachments) of the JusPrin Agent WebView, built on `jusprin-newui` on top of the tested Phases 1–4. See [[agent-bridge-phase-4]] for the persistence/revert design it extends.

**Protocol version pinned at 1** (see [[protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary]] — additive changes use capabilities, not a version bump; the initial v4 bump was reverted and the number reset to 1 as the pre-release baseline). Changes in `resources/jusprin/agent/protocol.json` + `AgentProtocol.hpp` + `AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts`, all cross-checked by one contract test: added capability `attachments`; page messages `attach_file`, `remove_attachment`; host message `attachment_updated`; `WireMessage.attachments` (ids) and `StatePayload.attachments` (`AttachmentInfo[]`, optional in TS). `user_message` now carries `attachmentIds` and allows empty text when an attachment is present.

**Storage.** Attachment metadata lives in `ProjectStateDocument` (`AttachmentRecord`, counter `nextAttachment`, id `a-<n>`, states staged|sent|error, clientId for resend dedup). Blobs live at `<aux>/JusPrin/attachments/<id>/<sanitized-name>` via `ProjectPersistence::write/read/remove_attachment_blob`. Clean-sharing drops attachments for free (export excludes all aux data). Revert copies kept blob dirs to scratch and back across the aux-dir move (restore replaces the project) and drops orphaned ones; `TruncateResult` gained removed/kept attachment dirs. Rule: staged survive revert; a sent attachment survives only if a surviving message still references it.

**Host** (`AgentHost.cpp`): base64 decode/encode, UTF-8 validation, extension→kind classification, `sanitize_filename` (no traversal), size cap 32MB, text preview cap 4000 chars, image preview cap 256KB. Image `previewDataUrl` is rebuilt on demand from the blob (NOT persisted in state.json, to avoid bloat/duplication); `previewText` IS persisted (small).

**Native import seam.** `IWorkspace::import_model(path)` (additive, undoable, one revision). Real `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::import_model` wraps `Plater::take_snapshot` + `load_files(paths, LoadStrategy::LoadModel)` in a `project_state_transaction` (nesting is supported — `restore_project_archive` relies on it). A sent model attachment → mock proposes an `import_model` tool (ActionClass::Mutation; approval was required then, removed 2026-10-07, see [[tool-call-approval-removed]]) → `ToolExecutionCoordinator` resolves the opaque attachmentId to an absolute path via a host-set resolver (no machine path persisted) → `workspace.import_model`. FakeWorkspace adds a synthetic object.

**Tradeoffs to revisit:** PDF is store+preview only (no text extraction — no provider consumes it yet); a rendered model thumbnail is deferred (needs GL, headless summary used instead); staged-but-unsent attachments would be embedded on an explicit Save (benign). Multiple model attachments: only the first is proposed for import.

**Tests:** native `agent_bridge_tests` 46→63 cases; vitest 35→42. Real `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::import_model` is verified only by full-build compilation, not runtime — needs manual acceptance in the app. Track long GUI builds by wall-clock per [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

**Correction 2026-10-14:** tool-call approval was removed on 2026-10-07 (eb45279cd5). See [[tool-call-approval-removed]].
===== protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary.md
---
name: protocol-version-only-at-compat-boundary
description: "Agent-bridge protocol version is pinned at 1 pre-release; add features via the capabilities list, never a version bump."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 05ae687e-7468-4101-ba4b-f0017c8876c5
  modified: 2026-09-01T07:39:46.979Z
---

For the JusPrin agent bridge, do NOT increment the protocol version integer for additive changes (new message types, new capabilities), and especially not before the product is released.

**Why:** the version integer exists only so a running web page and native host can detect they are incompatible. They are built together and baked into the same binary (the bundle ships inside `resources/jusprin/agent/index.html` in the same build as the host), and nothing is released — so no older peer exists that a version bump could protect. Feature detection is the job of the `capabilities` list, and additive changes are backward-compatible by construction.

**Baseline:** the version is pinned at **1** and stays 1 through all pre-release development. It bumps only after go-live, on a breaking change to an existing message's shape. (Kenny's call, 2026-09-01: the per-phase v1→v2→v3 bumps were all churn, so it was reset to 1.)

**How to apply:** add the new capability to `capabilities` (in `protocol.json`, `AgentProtocol.hpp`, and `protocol.ts` — the contract test checks all three agree) and the new message-type constants; leave `kVersion` at 1. Note `state.json` has its own separate `ProjectStateDocument::kSchemaVersion` — that IS a real persistence-compatibility concern (saved 3mf opened by another build) and is unrelated to this protocol version; don't conflate them.

name: agent-panel-css-namespaces
description: AgentUI styles.css has no CSS modules — the setup-* class prefix belongs to the agent setup screens, so new components need their own prefix
metadata:
  type: project
---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/styles.css` is one flat global stylesheet
with no CSS modules or scoping. The `setup-*` prefix is already taken by the
agent **setup screens** (`Setup.tsx`, `SetupLocalTool.tsx`) — `.setup-card`
there is `display: flex; flex-direction: column` on a lavender
`--surface-selected` ground.

**Why:** a new component that reuses one of those names silently inherits
`display: flex` and leaks its own rules back onto the setup screens. This cost
real time once: the "Current setup" card reused `.setup-card`, which defeated
its `white-space: nowrap` title clamp and re-tinted its background. Both
suites stayed green — jsdom does no layout, so no unit test can see it.

**How to apply:** pick a prefix that does not already appear in styles.css
(`grep -n '^\.<prefix>' src/styles.css`), and verify layout by rendering the
real component at real width rather than trusting tests. The pattern that
works: `SetupCard.preview.test.tsx` uses `renderToStaticMarkup` plus the real
styles.css and design tokens to emit a page of every state, served over a
local http server and measured in the browser (`scrollWidth > clientWidth`,
row heights). See [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].

name: prove-guard-tests-fail-first
description: A lint-style test that reads a source file must be shown failing on injected drift before it counts; Vitest hands CSS imports (even ?raw) back empty in the AgentUI setup.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

  originSessionId: 1b302f25-67a5-44d7-9f2c-02b68b2a0bb8

In `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI`, `import css from './styles.css?raw'` under Vitest resolves to an empty string, and `new URL('./x', import.meta.url)` is not a `file:` URL in the jsdom environment. A stylesheet-guard test written either way passed green while asserting nothing.

**Why:** Vitest's CSS handling short-circuits the import before Vite's `?raw` asset path runs, so every regex over the "stylesheet" matched nothing. Only appending a deliberate `border-radius: 4px` to the file and watching the suite stay green exposed it.

**How to apply:** Read source files in tests with `readFileSync(join(__dirname, ...))` and assert the text is non-empty. For any guard test that scans a file, inject the violation it exists to catch, confirm it fails naming the offender, then restore. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[fork-rebase-risk-verify-before-claiming]].

===== jusprin-worktree-build.md
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

name: fake-host-page-fixture

metadata:

Both pages find their host through `window.wx.postMessage(json)` and receive host
envelopes through `window.__jusprinBridge.deliver(envelope)` (`WebShared/bridgeClient.ts`).
Copy `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` to a scratch dir, inject
`<script>` right after `<head>` that (1) defines `window.wx` answering `hello` with
`hello_ack` + a full `state`, and (2) exposes `window.fake.deliver(type, payload)`;
serve with `python3 -m http.server` and open `agent.html?panel=printer` /
`home.html` via `preview_start`. Drive it with `javascript_tool`: deliver
`assistant_started` with no `assistant_delta` to freeze a streaming empty turn,
`printer_session` to pin a card, `printer_added` for Home's receipt strip. A file
drop works with `new DragEvent('drop', {dataTransfer})` on `.app--printer`.
Envelope: `{protocol:'jusprin-agent-bridge'|'jusprin-home-bridge', version:1, id, type, payload}`.
Used 2026-09-19 to review branch these-commits-are-probably-wrong in ~10 minutes.

**Why:** the desktop tools were locked by another session and background
`app_click` never reaches WKWebView content, so page-level states (streaming
activity line, compact photo chip, leave dialog, receipt strip) had no other cheap
proof. It proves page rendering only; host behaviour (e.g. the 256 KiB image
preview cap `kInlineImagePreviewCap` in `AgentHost.cpp`) must be replicated in
the fake by hand or checked live.

**How to apply:** reach for this before building a full app + datadir copy when the
question is "what does the page draw for state X". Pair with [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]]
for the host side. Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]].
===== prompt-eval-spend-budget.md
---
name: prompt-eval-spend-budget
description: No live-model prompt tests without Kenneth approving a specific batch; my stub run-to-the-end design burned 300M+ tokens and the OpenRouter monthly limit (2026-10-10).
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-08 to 10 my live prompt tests used more than 300M tokens on the OpenRouter key (`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env`) and hit its monthly limit. Kenneth's verdict on 2026-10-10: letting the agent wander on stub replies for 16 requests was a stupid design. I agree.

What went wrong, specifically:
- Every request carries about 10k input tokens (prompt plus 29 tool definitions); with `store:false` every tool call resends all of it plus the history.
- About 1,300 runs were "stub tools, run to the end": I removed the stop line from `tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`'s loop and let conversations continue to a 16-request cap on its canned replies (`workspace_result`: six tools get a fixed answer, the rest `{"accepted": true}`). The replies never answer the model's question, so it wandered 10–19 calls; about 150–200k tokens per run, 195–260M in total. The simulator runs (about 630, about 40M) and first-step runs (about 500, about 12M) were the cheap part.
- It began as a one-off shortcut, I kept it "for comparability", then chased its noise with more runs. The scripts logged no usage.

**Why:** the money, and the numbers were also bad: most unrequested slices came after about 15 empty reads, so the test partly provoked what it counted.

**How to apply (Kenneth's instructions, 2026-10-10):**
- Run no live-model tests until Kenneth approves a specific batch. A `403 Key limit exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys or route around it.
- Never run conversations to the end on canned tool replies. Use the stateful simulator (`run_workflow_tests.py`, `workflow_fixture.py`) and the committed first-step test (stops at the first tool call, 8-request cap). If more varied full conversations are needed, extend the simulator so replies answer what was asked.
- Before a batch: state runs × tokens (about 65k per simulator run, about 25k per first-step run), one control, one round. Log `usage` from every response and report the actual total.
- Keep stub-derived rates out of the repo and out of reports.

Related: [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]].

metadata:

On 2026-10-15 Kenneth reviewed my nozzle-change proposal. It had per-cause error messages, prompt rules and handling for save failures caused by a full disk, an open paint tool or a not-yet-drawn canvas. He said those cases were wrong, speculative or rare, and that they should simply get a generic error.

**Why:** they are hard to handle well and almost never happen. The effort belongs on failures people actually hit, like the printer panel's action-id collision, which I reproduced.

**How to apply:** before proposing handling for a failure, ask whether a real person will plausibly hit it. If it's rare or unreproduced, recommend the existing generic error and move on. Don't list speculative causes as if they were findings. Related: [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]], [[printer-panel-action-id-collision]].
===== rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs.md

name: rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs
description: "Kenneth's one-home rule, corrected 2026-10-15 — a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; a rule about the conversation lives in the prompt. Not \"all policy in the prompt\"."
metadata:

---

A rule lives once, as close as possible to the thing it governs: a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; a rule about the conversation (when to act, when to ask, record intent before preparing, reply language) lives in the prompt.

**Why:** the 2026-10-14 handoff turned "one home per rule" into "the prompt is the home". Applied in 2595f0556c, that stripped one-tool rules (skipped_confirmation settling, export slice check, project_open's message handling, intent_update's "do not infer") out of descriptions, which every caller sees — project, printer and filament chats and MCP clients — and left the other chats and MCP with nothing. The old reason for prompt-side policy, tool deferral hiding descriptions, is gone. Kenneth endorsed the correction on 2026-10-15.

**How to apply:** ask "who needs this rule?" A rule about one tool's arguments or output goes in its description even if it says "ask" or "explain". Check the host's per-turn lines before calling them a rule's home: the "file-load reports are source data" developer line exists only for files the person opened, not for project_open called by the model or for MCP. Also: asking the person when the answer is theirs (which printer they own, which project to continue) is wanted and important; the 2026-10-07 removal was of approval gates on tool calls, not of asking. Related: [[tool-call-approval-removed]], [[project-prompt-sections]], [[orca-edit-questions-forwarded]].

commit 170d1ae080839b7aaa6cec4dc5ee9447588cb3a5
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Oct 19 18:19:35 2026 -0700

    Add Anthropic and OpenRouter as Agent providers behind one provider-neutral turn loop
    
    The in-app Agent talked to one API, OpenAI's Responses API, through
    OpenAIResponsesAgent, which mixed the tool-call turn loop with that
    wire format and with OpenAI-specific choices. Adding a second provider
    would have meant a second copy of the loop.
    
    ProviderAgent now owns the loop and a provider-neutral transcript: the
    instructions, the tools offered, the earlier conversation, this turn's
    user content, and one step per response holding the provider's own
    record of its reply (kept verbatim, because both OpenAI and Anthropic
    want it echoed back unchanged) with the results of the calls it made.
    Every rule the old class enforced is unchanged: calls run one at a time
    in the order written, a failed call answers the rest unrun, unknown or
    invalid calls are refused back at most twice a turn, images follow
    results, fired skills are sent once on OpenAI, and late events from a
    cancelled request are dropped.
    
    A codec per API family turns that transcript into a request and each
    streamed payload into neutral events. ResponsesCodec serves OpenAI and
    OpenRouter; its request bodies are byte-identical to the old adapter's,
    checked against the shell harness's recorded bodies. AnthropicCodec
    serves the Messages API: system and tool cache breakpoints, tool_use and
    tool_result replay, same-role merging, images inside tool results, call
    arguments assembled from streamed fragments, every stop reason mapped,
    and the keywords Anthropic's strict mode rejects (minimum, maximum,
    minLength, maxLength, maxItems) moved from each tool's schema into the
    property description, so the registry keeps its full schemas for native
    validation and for MCP clients. On Anthropic a fired skill stays in place
    on later requests of the same turn, because dropping it counts as editing
    history and Opus 5.5 then rejects replayed thinking.
    
    Providers are data in ProviderProfile: family, endpoint, auth header,
    fixed headers, default model, output limit and display name. OpenRouter
    defaults to the same model as OpenAI; Anthropic to claude-opus-5-5 with
    a 64000-token output limit. Setup and configuration build the agent
    through one factory keyed by provider, and JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT
    overrides whichever endpoint is active (JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT still
    works). The setup page offers OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic, with
    OpenAI still the default tab. OpenAIResponsesAgent remains as a thin
    subclass so the harness compiles unchanged.
    
    Tests: the adapter tests are split into loop tests driven through a
    scripted fake codec and wire tests per codec; a conformance test drives
    one scripted turn through both codecs and requires identical events;
    unit tests cover the schema projection. test_provider_live.cpp holds
    metered live smokes that skip without a key and refuse any request that
    could cross a $0.50 cap. Their first runs are recorded there: OpenRouter,
    4 requests, $0.0107; Anthropic, 7 requests, $0.0886, including the
    history check with a fired skill, OpenAI-minted call ids in replayed
    history, and both title-request shapes.
    
    The tool registry, ToolExecutionCoordinator, AgentHost and the MCP
    server are unchanged.
